answer: In a comet-image market, each paid key seals a separate 192-GiB chained archive at a haven relay; each page depends on its predecessor and that key’s salt. A surprise jetty audit asks all keys for 256 random pages within two seconds. Independent receivers time replies; proposed validators check roots, denying payout for late or reused pages. A farm can rent disks and share its model, but cannot derive missing pages from one shared archive in time: each extra key needs another resident 192 GiB plus simultaneous reads. This needs new validators, not MinePoA rules.
